comment_verbatim: The focus on CD8 T cells is briefly explained (lines 100-104) but it still seems odd that the investigators did not perform any substantial analyses of any other cell lineages (CD4 T cells, B cells, monocytes, DCs, NK cells etc). response: Differential expression and pathway enrichment were run for all 30 annotated populations across five contrasts (148 per-population tables under Analysis/Differential_Expression/, 146 enrichment workbooks under Analysis/Pathway_Analysis/); volcano plots for a subset are Supplementary Figures 6, 7 and 9C. CD4: Myc targets V2 significant in CD4 only in the infection contrast (Naive 1, p_adj 5.3e-07); E2F targets and DNA repair significant in CD4 only in the exposure contrast; G2-M checkpoint and mitotic spindle significant in CD4 only in the treatment contrast. CD4 carries the largest burden of any lineage. Monocyte: complement significant only in monocytes, HEU-versus-HUU contrast (classical p_adj 7.3e-07, non-classical 1.3e-03); IL-6/JAK/STAT3 concurrent (1.2e-03). Coagulation significant only in monocytes in the infection contrast (1.7e-04), separating exposed-uninfected from unexposed infants. B cell: fatty acid metabolism significant only in B cells (transitional, activated, resting naive subsets) in the infection contrast (p_adj 2.5e-02 to 2.9e-02); heme metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis significant only in B cells in the exposure contrast. NK, gamma-delta T, MAIT: NK shows two lineage-specific terms (G2-M checkpoint p_adj 2.9e-02, estrogen response early 4.4e-02). Gamma-delta T has no Hallmark term unique to it in any of the five contrasts. MAIT shows 27 significant calls in the viraemia contrast. pDC: no results in any of the five contrasts. comment_verbatim: The authors have an opportunity here to look for HIV-infected cells in their dataset by realigning to a combined human/HIV reference, which would substantially strengthen the paper.
response: Nine entry-visit libraries were realigned with Cell Ranger 10.1.0 to a combined GRCh38 + HIV-1 reference carrying subtype B (HXB2) and subtype C contigs. We detected 1,473 HIV-1 UMIs in 32 cells. The signal is concentrated: 1,444 of the 1,473 UMIs are carried by five cells, and the three largest carry 780, 334 and 289 UMIs. The two of those retained in the annotated object are effector-memory CD4 T cells (Th2/Th17 EM CD4), in which HIV-1 accounts for 16.6% and 4.6% of the host transcriptome; the third was removed by quality-control filtering and carries no lineage label. The remaining 27 cells carry one or two UMIs each, 29 UMIs in total, distributed across eight lineages including B and NK cells. Three controls distinguish this signal from ambient vRNA. Cell-associated UMIs account for 98.0%, 96.3% and 79.6% of total vRNA in CP017_2m, CP016_2m and CP002_1m; the six remaining libraries yield 0-3 cell-associated UMIs (0-5 in total). Of the 5 cells carrying three or more UMIs, 2 carry a lineage label and both are effector-memory CD4 T cells; the other 3 were removed by quality-control filtering and are unannotated. Cells carrying one or two UMIs show no lineage restriction. Subtype B contigs account for the majority of cell-associated UMIs in all three positive libraries. vRNA yield does not track plasma viral load: CP022_1m, the highest in the cohort at 5.08 x 10^6 copies/mL, yields three UMIs. Libraries below the evaluable threshold are negative at this detection ceiling, which is not equivalent to absence of infected cells. The panel and the per-library table were added, under Reviewer_Comments/Figures (github.com/codeneeded/CD8_Longitudinal).

comment_verbatim: It is not clear from the Methods how the Module Score was calculated.

TEMRA/CTL is the population that differs: HEI vs HEU p = 0.022, HEI vs HUU p = 0.026. This panel was added.

comment_verbatim: CD8 cluster frequencies should be expressed as a percentage of total CD8 cells rather than of live cells.
response: Cluster frequency as a percentage of total CD8 is reported in Supplementary Figure 1H alongside the percentage of total PBMC. TEMRA/CTL differs between HEU and HEI under both denominators (p = 0.011); the remaining five clusters do not reach p < 0.05 (Naive 1 p = 0.88, Naive 2 p = 0.060, Naive Intermediate p = 0.23, Tscm p = 0.13, Tex p = 0.17). The second denominator was added.

comment_verbatim: A CD16+ effector CD8 population has been described in congenital CMV infection (PMID 39531313).
response: The CD16+ effector CD8 population (860 cells, 4.6% of CD8) matches the phenotype reported in Semmes et al. (J Clin Invest 2024;135(1), PMID 39531313) on all 11 testable features. T-bet is higher (46.4% vs 15.8% of cells) and BCL11B is lower (45.1% vs 59.9%). CD57, PD-1 and NKG2C are elevated (4.7 vs 1.1%, 10.6 vs 4.5%, 35.1 vs 17.0%). PRF1 86.9 vs 33.6%, GNLY 95.1 vs 32.1%, NKG7 98.5 vs 42.4%. Gamma-delta TCR: 37.0% here vs a reported median of 19%. Database-predicted CMV-specific clonotypes: 4.65% vs 10.88% of TCR-recovered cells (Fisher OR 0.39, p = 5.2e-11); alpha-beta-restricted, OR 0.47, p = 1.5e-05. TEMRA CD8 gamma-delta fraction: 37.1%. CMV association not attributed; population not attributed to HIV exposure. Added to the Discussion (tracked edit under R2-M3d, p. 23, ll. 603–613). The signature comparison panel and its table were added, under Reviewer_Comments/Figures (github.com/codeneeded/CD8_Longitudinal).

comment_verbatim: The claim of renewable anti-HIV CD8 potential is not supported and should rest on the FACT-Seq data.
response: FACT-Seq identifies HIV-reactive clonotypes functionally, by proliferation on HIV peptide stimulation, in two participants with different treatment histories. HIV-reactive clonotypes persist and remain peptide-responsive across years of follow-up, including in a participant sampled before treatment initiation. Comparing each participant against their own non-specific cells, four of five functional programmes behave concordantly while Type I interferon memory inverts between the suppressed and unsuppressed participant. This qualification was added.
